nodes.title: Note: FastH3 Omni
widgets_values:
## FastH3 Omni - Reference to Video + Audio (8 steps)

FastVideo's distilled MiniMax H3 (built with Nuva Lab): give it **pictures, a video or audio as references** and a prompt, and it makes a video WITH synchronized sound in **8 steps**. Sparse attention (VSA) is trained into the model, so it is fast without any extra patch.

**How to use**
- **Picture 1** (User Inputs): your character, product or scene. Use a full-size picture.
- Fast Groups Muter: switch on **Picture 2** (a second reference, e.g. a location), **Reference Video** (2-15 s; its look and motion), **Your Audio** (a voice line: the character lip-syncs to YOUR audio, played 1:1) or the **RTX 2x Upscale**.
- Resolution Selector: 0.6 MP for 12 GB cards; 1 MP for more detail. Pick the aspect ratio of your result (it does not need to match the picture).
- Write the prompt in the format of the example (see the Prompt Guide note): name every reference with its tag, e.g. <Picture 1>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1>.

**Required settings (already set):** 8 steps, euler + simple, guidance 1.0, MiniMax Sigma Shift 12 (video) / 3 (audio), Model Sparse Attention method vsa, keep 10 %. Do not use the FastH3 text-to-video shift (10) here.

**Speed tip:** PyTorch built for CUDA 13 (cu130, the standard nvidia portable build) with an NVIDIA driver 580+. On cu128 ComfyUI turns its fast kernels off.

On my test GPU (RTX 4000 Ada, 20 GB), a 5 s clip at 0.6 MP sampled in about 1:50, and with a 12 GB VRAM limit it still ran at full speed (peak 11.3 GB). 1 MP took about 3:05 under a 13.5 GB limit (peak 12.8 GB). A reference video adds a lot of time (a 5 s video reference took 11:42 at 0.8 MP).

Model by FastVideo + Nuva Lab, based on MiniMax H3 by MiniMax; ComfyUI template by Comfy-Org. Licence: MiniMax-H3 Community License (read it: it limits where outputs may be used). Video by TheLocalLab: youtube.com/@TheLocalLab

nodes.title: Note: Model Links
widgets_values:
## Model Links

**FastH3 Omni** (FastVideo) - https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastH3-Omni-Comfy/tree/main
- diffusion_models/fasth3_omniref_8step_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors (~22 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/
  - or the bf16 version (~44 GB) if you have the RAM

**Text encoder + VAEs** (same files as MiniMax H3) - https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main
- text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors (~16 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/
  - fast NVFP4 needs an RTX 50 series card; it also runs on older cards (we use it on RTX 30/40-class GPUs). The int8 version (~27 GB) is the other option.
- vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors (~2.8 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/vae/
- vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors (~0.6 GB) -> ComfyUI/models/vae/ (needed for the sound)

**Custom nodes:** the main nodes are built into ComfyUI (update to the latest version). For the optional groups: VideoHelperSuite (reference video, 2x save), Nvidia RTX Nodes (upscale), rgthree (group switch). Install with ComfyUI Manager -> Install Missing Custom Nodes.

nodes.title: Input Text (Prompt)
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the setting in <Picture 1>: a vast futuristic hangar with glowing blue floor lines, mist, a sleek white shuttle and huge windows showing a red planet.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a 5-second, two-shot sci-fi clip. The shuttle in <Subject 1> powers up and lifts off toward the window and the red planet.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - the hangar, blue floor lines, white shuttle and red planet window are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a cinematic, high-contrast sci-fi scene with volumetric light.
[Shot 1] A wide shot matches <Picture 1>: mist drifts across the floor as the blue lines pulse and the white shuttle's engines start to glow.
[Shot 2] At 00:02.500, the shot cuts to a low angle as the shuttle lifts off, hovers for a moment, then glides toward the huge window and the red planet.

overall_soundscape:
The deep hum of the hangar, a rising engine whine and a heavy rumble at lift-off.

non_diegetic_music:
A low cinematic synth swell.

nodes.title: Note: Sizes and Speed
widgets_values:
## Sizes and Speed

| megapixels | 16:9 | 9:16 | 1:1 | 2:3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6 | 1056 x 608 | 608 x 1056 | 768 x 768 | 640 x 960 |
| 0.8 | 1216 x 672 | 672 x 1216 | 896 x 896 | 736 x 1120 |
| 1.0 | 1376 x 768 | 768 x 1376 | 1024 x 1024 | 832 x 1248 |

Measured on an RTX 4000 Ada (20 GB), 5 s, 8 steps, sparse attention on: 0.6 MP about 1:50-2:07 (12 GB limit: full speed, peak 11.3 GB); 1 MP about 3:05-3:14 (peak 12.8 GB under a 13.5 GB limit). A full Task Manager is normal: ComfyUI fills free VRAM on purpose.

Duration: 5 s = 124 frames (the model's trained range is about 5-15 s). The RTX 2x Upscale group doubles the final size.

nodes.title: Reference video (2-15 s; its look and motion)
Your audio (the exact line the character speaks)
Note: Prompt Guide
widgets_values:
## Prompt Guide (the format FastH3 Omni was trained on)

Name each reference with its tag in the order they are connected: <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1>.

**One picture -> new scene, two shots** (the example in this workflow: the hangar): subject_definitions (who/what is in <Picture 1>), summary starting with [reference generation], retention_analysis (what must stay the same), detailed_description with [Shot 1] (and [Shot 2] at 00:02.500 for a cut), overall_soundscape (the sounds you want), non_diegetic_music (N/A or a style).

**Lip-sync to YOUR audio** (switch on "Your Audio"; your line is played 1:1):
- subject_definitions: add "<Audio 1> is the complete dialogue track for <Subject 1> (S1), a clear spoken English male voice."
- summary: start with [reference generation + audio reuse]
- retention_analysis: add "<Audio 1>: fully_copy - <Audio 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track."
- detailed_description: write the exact words inside <d>[English] ...</d>, e.g. <Subject 1> (S1) looks into the camera and says, <d>[English] Your exact line here.</d> Then he closes his mouth and nods.
- Make the clip at least as long as your audio (pad the audio with silence to the clip length).

**Reference video:** "<Subject 1> is the fox in <Video 1>: ..." then describe the NEW scene. The video sets the look and motion; it is not copied.

Tips: one clear action per shot; describe the sounds you want; end each spoken line with a period.
